newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares finish shade higher, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares finish shade higher, profit-taking.

text.p: Share prices at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ended slightly higher on Wednesday after late profit-taking wiped out a strong market rally, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share BSE index was up 6.62 points at a provisional 3,344.35 close, below the day's high of 3,373.51.
"The first day of settlement at the National Stock Exchange led to some selective buying by operators," said Vijay Pandya of Classic Share & Stock Brokers.
He said reports that the State Bank of India's (SBI) $400 million GDR offering had received a good response at its road shows buoyed the market helping pivotals climb higher.
SBI's GDR issue had apparently received firm offers for over $300 million and is likely to be priced at a premium, brokers said.
A Reuter poll of 14 leading securities firms, on Tuesday, shows SBI posting a 177.7 percent surge in its net profit for the six months ended September 30, 1996.
Traders said foreign funds were select buyers in Hindustan Lever, MTNL, SBI, India Cements, TELCO, Hindalco, IDBI and Nalco.
The 50-stock national bourse index gained 1.82 points or 0.19 percent at a provisional 970.82. The 500-share CRISIL index fell 1.23 points to 649.33.
"Only select stocks saw improved volumes but higher levels continued to attract sellers," a trader said.
SBI rose 1.75 rupees to 264.25, TELCO 2.0 to 459.50, MTNL 3.75 to 217.0, ITC 1.75 to 300.0 and HDFC 26.50 to 432.0.
Reliance and Hindustan Lever were unchanged at 197.0 rupees and 826.0 respectively. Losing stocks included ACC down 16.25 rupees at 1,853 rupees and TISCO 1.0 at 172.50.
